speaker: john_heminges
text: We sup on the boxes, and I would rather say the figure while the mutton is hot. Item, seven pound eleven. Item, this table. The one can bear the other.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then let it bear it, John. I have already had the sum once, in the tiring-parlour. I am glad to have it again from you, because you do not garnish a total.

speaker: george_bryan
text: The Inns were on the stair, term or no term. I began to count caps and I stopped, which is the correct use of me. Margery's sort of counting is the one that comes to a penny. Mine comes to a mood.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Thou sawest the quiet, Will. I have played comedies that sent them out louder than they came in. I do not know what to do with the other kind, except eat.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Eat, then. I saw it. I am not building a moral over a supper that has not yet been served. Dick, thou wert good. That is as much praise as the mutton can carry.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Item, praise, which I do not enter. Item, the watchet, fifty shillings, still the mercer's. Tonight does not pay him. I am saying it now so that a good house does not become a story in which we are suddenly clear.

speaker: george_bryan
text: The boy wore it as if it were clear. That is Nick's gift, and it is not a receipt. I am content to be in debt for a blue that held, provided John has written the debt and not the contentment.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The debt is written. The contentment is your department, George. Item, Edith's eight shillings, still unpaid, and not this supper's to settle. I will not have a good Thursday pay an old bill by accident.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave both bills. I did not come to clear them. I came because the boxes were strong enough for a meal, and because I wanted the four of us at a table before the day turned into a report.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Then report nothing. Thou went on in paper and old velvet, and the first line survived thee, which is a compliment. The rhymes held. Pope stopped us twice and the yard forgave him in laughter. I can say all that and still want the bread.

speaker: george_bryan
text: The bread is here. So is the quiet, sitting among us like a guest who will not drink. I am not afraid of it. I am only unused to a new play ending without a shove.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: There was no shove. There was a messenger, and a pause, and they went out. George, if you are unused to it, keep the unused. Do not cure it with a speech.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Item, no speech. I am in favour. Seven pound eleven, less nothing we have not yet spent. I am not dividing shares at a supper. Saturday is the reckoning. Tonight is the mutton.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Saturday, then. Thou wilt be there, Will, and thou wilt take what is thine without a joke, if I know thee. Tonight thou mayst be pleased. I give thee leave. I rarely have the chance.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am pleased. The ladies had the better of it, and the yard did not fight them for it. That is enough pleasure for a Thursday. I will not spend it in advance on Saturday's arithmetic.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Anne will have the plot in four lines, I suppose, when the carrier goes. You will tell her the ladies won. You are a better husband in a letter than you are at this table, where you keep a chair empty as if a fifth man might improve us.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The letter is already written. It waits for the twenty-seventh. I do not want a fifth man. Sit, George. Four is the supper that was set.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The— the second cut of the mutton is Dick's, who has talked enough to have earned it, and a cup for George, who stopped a count at the right time.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: I accept the cut. Thou, Will, eat before it cools. A quiet yard will not feed you. Seven pound eleven will, and only by way of this plate.

speaker: george_bryan
text: To the boxes, then, and not to our own wisdom. I can drink to a sum. I am less sure I can drink to a silence. John, is the cup actually coming, or is it another item?

speaker: john_heminges
text: The cup is coming. I do not itemise a cup that is in my hand. Seven pound eleven. A good house. An unpaid gown. An unpaid eight shillings. And this meal. That is the state of the company at half past six, and I am content to stop.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Then I will drink the cup, and I will stop making a guest of the silence. It is a quiet yard. It has already happened.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Thou art learning, George. The bread is the last thing I mean to argue for.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Item, bread. I have already said the rest.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Stop, then. I am content with the same list. Let the parlour stay a parlour for a little. I have had enough of the yard for one day, and not enough of the bread.
